rows.scope: Public water systems, primary MCLs in Table 64431-A (22 CCR § 64431), row "Chromium (hexavalent)"; compliance applies to community and nontransient-noncommunity systems with transient-noncommunity monitoring per § 64432(o)
rows.basis: concentration in drinking water, Maximum Contaminant Level in mg/L (0.010 mg/L = 10 µg/L; taken as 10 µg/kg for water)
rows.evidence: "Chromium (hexavalent) 0.010" — Table 64431-A, Maximum Contaminant Level, mg/L; § 64431, p.2 of 16
rows.primary_source_used: https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/drinking_water/certlic/drinkingwater/docs/2024/cr6-mcl-final-regulation-text.pdf (SWRCB "Final Regulation Text", 16 pp, PDF created 2024-07-25); corroborated by held copy raw/regulatory/us-ca/ca-swrcb-hexavalent-chromium-mcl-regulation-text-2024.pdf (February 2024 proposed text, 17 pp, same Table 64431-A value) and by https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/drinking_water/certlic/drinkingwater/SWRCBDDW-21-003_hexavalent_chromium.html for dates
rows.note: 0.010 mg/L × 1000 = 10 µg/L; matches 10 µg/kg on a water basis. In-force evidence from the SWRCB rulemaking page (SWRCB-DDW-21-003): adopted 2024-04-17 by Resolution 2024-0015, OAL approved 2024-07-24, effective 2024-10-01; no stay, litigation or amendment noted. Compliance is phased by Table 64432-B: systems with 10,000+ service connections by 2026-10-01, 1,000-9,999 by 2027-10-01, fewer than 1,000 by 2028-10-01, so as of 2026-09-02 the MCL is in force but no system's compliance date has yet arrived. The raw/ held copy is the February 2024 proposed text (footer "Regulation Text (proposed)", Table 64432-B still has [INSERT DATE] placeholders); the SWRCB final text carries the same 0.010 mg/L and the filled-in dates. The final text is not yet held in raw/regulatory.

rows.scope: Eleventh Schedule, Part A "Maximum permitted levels of chemical contaminants", paragraph (15) lead in fish and fisheries products: "Muscle meat of fish, excluding those listed below" (the listed exceptions are bonito, horse mackerel/scad, sardine, sardinops, spotted seabass, tuna at 0.4; crustaceans 0.5; cephalopods 1.0)
rows.basis: Max Level in mg/Kg as printed; the instrument states no wet/dry or as-sold qualifier; Reg 30(2): non-compliant when any one sample unit exceeds the Schedule level
rows.evidence: "Muscle meat of fish, excluding those listed below. 0.2" — Eleventh Schedule A para (15), Max Level (mg/Kg); held copy PDF p.107 of 202
rows.primary_source_used: raw/regulatory/fj/fiji-food-safety-regulations-2009-chemical-contaminants.pdf (sha256 96f00728…, byte-identical to the Fiji Ministry of Health copy at https://www.health.gov.fj/wp-content/uploads/2014/09/33_The-Food-Safety-Regulations-2009.pdf); independently confirmed in the FAOLEX gazette scan https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/fij110379.pdf; amendment L.N. 89/2010 read at https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/fij110380.pdf
rows.note: 0.2 mg/Kg × 1000 = 200 µg/kg; matches. Register defect: the row URL (https://biotech.law.lsu.edu/obesity/who/report_food_safety_consultation.pdf) is NOT the instrument; it is the WHO-WPRO report of the FAO/SPC/WHO Pacific Islands Food Safety and Quality Consultation, Nadi, 11-15 Nov 2002 (59 pp, 2003), which contains no Fiji schedule or lead limit; verification used the held copy instead. In-force basis: Reg 1(2) commences the Regulations on Gazette publication; L.N. 89/2010 s.1(2) records that commencement date as 5 June 2009; InforMEA/ECOLEX list the instrument as in force (not repealed), amended by L.N. 89/2010, L.N. 35/2014 and L.N. 19/2019. L.N. 89/2010 was read in full: it only inserts new Eleventh Schedule paragraphs (25) dioxins/PCBs, (26) PAH and (27) inorganic tin 200 ppm in canned foods, and leaves paragraph (15) untouched. The texts of L.N. 35/2014 (described in secondary records as nutrition-labelling) and L.N. 19/2019 (content unknown) could not be obtained: laws.gov.fj sits behind an "I Agree" disclaimer gate that was not clicked, and FAOLEX/PacLII/fao.org blocked or bot-gated the fetch; residual risk that a later amendment altered para (15) is unverified. Instrument quirks: the Eleventh Schedule header misprints "FOOD SAFETY REGULATIONS 2008" and cites "(Regulation 28 (1))" while the operative provision is Reg 30(1). The register basis field holds a unit ("mg/Kg"), not a basis.
